facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, which are characteristic findings of blepharitis.
The patient has ectropic lower eyelids, which is a key feature of ectropion.
The patient has biopsy-proven Crohn disease and was initially on infliximab therapy, which is a common treatment for Crohn disease.
The patient has diffuse conjunctival hyperemia, which may be related to an underlying autoimmune disorder, and the presence of Crohn disease, which is an autoimmune condition.
It explains the finding of diffuse conjunctival hyperemia and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins in the context of normal visual acuity.

rationales.F01: Crohn disease is a known risk factor for various extraintestinal manifestations, including ocular inflammation.
rationales.F04: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids are characteristic of blepharitis.
rationales.F05: Ectropion is a known complication of blepharitis and other ocular conditions.
rationales.F07: Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are a common finding in blepharitis.
